title: DevEx: SDK guides, Quickstarts, API examples, and Top Support Issues (Playbook)
author: Aisha Rahman
summary: Canonical playbook for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and top support issues with canonical fixes.
body:
Overview

This playbook defines standards, templates, and operational procedures for Developer Experience documentation maintained by the DevEx team. It covers three correlated streams: SDK guides, Quickstarts & Templates, and API Examples, plus the docs-site operating procedures and the canonical fixes for top support issues. Use this document as the single source of truth for creating, reviewing, and operating public-facing developer docs and internal support runbooks.

Scope

- SDK Guides (Python, TypeScript, Go)
- Quickstarts & Templates (getting-started repos, IaC snippets)
- API Examples (REST + SDK patterns, streaming, function/tool-calling)
- Docs-site Operating Procedures (publishing, rollback, health checks)
- Top Support Issues and Canonical Fixes (triage playbook)

Ownership and Contacts

- Primary owner: DevEx (eng-developer-experience)
- Docs repo: github.com/redwood-inference/devex-docs (owner: devex-docs)
- Pager/Slack: #devex-docs (primary), #platform-ops (escalation)
- On-call: rotate weekly (see /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks for schedule)

Standards (applies to all assets)

1) Writing style
- Complete sentences, second-person where actionable ("Call the API...").
- Use short code examples that are copy-paste runnable.
- All examples must pin SDK versions (e.g., python: 0.9.3) and include dependency snippets.

2) Organization
- Each doc must include: Summary, Quickstart, Full guide, Examples, Troubleshooting, References.
- Use the standard header metadata (title, summary, owners, reviewers, created_at, last_updated).

3) Security and PII
- Never include production API keys or customer data. Use placeholders like <YOUR_API_KEY>.

SDK Guides: structure and checklist

- Goal: help engineers integrate Redwood SDKs within 5-15 minutes.
- Languages: Python, TypeScript, Go (prioritized).
- Each SDK guide MUST include:
  - Installation (pip/npm/go get)
  - Authentication snippet (KMS/HSM note for Private deployments)
  - Minimal example: single request + streaming example (if applicable)
  - Error handling patterns (retry backoff code sample)
  - Performance tips: batching, cache keys, concurrency sample (tokio/async examples where relevant)

Checklist (add to PR description):
- [ ] Example runs locally with pinned SDK version
- [ ] Code is <=50 lines for quickstart
- [ ] Security review if feature touches keys or telemetry
- [ ] Docs linter: markdownlint + spellcheck pass

Quickstarts & Templates

Purpose: reduce time-to-first-success with reference apps and templates.

Template types:
- Minimal API quickstart (1-file): shows auth and single generate call.
- Chat + tool-calling quickstart (multi-file): router + function stubs.
- Embeddings + similarity search (sample dataset & Faiss/pgvector snippets).
- IaC template for Dedicated/Private: Terraform module snippet and required env vars.

Repository layout convention (for quickstarts)
- /quickstarts/<name>/README.md (must include TL;DR, steps)
- /quickstarts/<name>/app/* (runnable app)
- /quickstarts/<name>/ci.yaml (simple GitHub Actions to validate)

API Examples

- Provide both REST and SDK variants for each pattern.
- Patterns to cover:
  - Basic text generation (sync + streaming)
  - Chat with system/instruction roles
  - Function/tool calling examples (with typed JSON schema)
  - Embeddings lifecycle: create, upsert, search, similarity threshold examples
  - Reranking flow with candidate scoring

Code example (Python, minimal):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="<YOUR_API_KEY>")
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-3b", prompt="Summarize: ...")
print(resp.text)
```

Docs-site Operating Procedures

Publishing flow:
1) Author opens a PR in devex-docs repo, adds metadata and checklist.
2) Two reviewers required (one DevEx, one subject-matter).
3) CI must pass (lint + unit examples + quickstart smoke tests).
4) Merge -> automated deploy to staging docs site (docs-staging.redwood.com).
5) Smoke test on staging (see below).
6) Promote to prod during 9:00-17:00 PT unless emergency.

Rollback procedure:
- If post-deploy regression is detected (see monitoring thresholds), revert the merge commit and redeploy. Notify #devex-docs and page on-call.

Smoke tests (automated):
- Health endpoint: GET /health -> 200 within 500ms
- Example-run: run 3 minimal quickstarts against a sandbox key (<=2s each)
- Static link check: no 404s in primary nav

Operational SLOs and KPIs (Docs site + DevEx assets)

- Docs site uptime: 99.9% monthly (measured by uptime monitors).
- Quickstart CI pass rate: >=95% (per week).
- PR review SLA: 48 hours for non-blocking changes, 4 hours for SEV issues.
- Incident-to-doc-update time: Top 5 support issues should have canonical doc/update within 24 hours of issue triage.

Top Support Issues and Canonical Fixes (current top-10)

Issue 1: "Auth errors: invalid api key / 401"
- Cause: customers using expired sandbox keys or copying example keys.
- Canonical fix: Update quickstarts to show environment variable usage and add troubleshooting section: check REDWOOD_API_KEY, ensure key has "docs-sandbox" scope.
- Example troubleshooting steps (to include in docs):
  1. Confirm env var: `echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY`
  2. Verify key scopes: contact platform-support@redwood.com
  3. Sample curl to validate: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.com/v1/health`

Issue 2: "Large-response streaming stalls"
- Cause: client-side stream buffer limits or incompatible proxies.
- Canonical fix: Provide streaming examples for popular HTTP clients (requests/urllib3, node-fetch, fetch in browser), recommend chunk-buffer sizes, and add a note about corporate proxies (MTU/timeouts).

Issue 3: "Embedding indexing mismatch / similarity returns wrong results"
- Cause: normalization differences between client vector store and Redwood embedding config.
- Canonical fix: Include explicit embedding configs (model, dimension, normalization step) in embeddings quickstart and provide canonical SQL for pgvector and example Faiss index code.

Issue 4: "SDK upgrade breaks existing code"
- Cause: breaking changes without migration guide.
- Canonical fix: Maintain CHANGELOG.md with migration snippets, and a compatibility table at top of SDK guides. Require feature-flagged rollout for major changes.

(Additional issues 5-10 included in appendix with repros and patches)

Release and Rollout Process for Docs Changes

- Patch (typo/security): can merge with one reviewer during business hours.
- Minor (content/clarity): two reviewers, automated CI.
- Major (API change / behavioral): require sign-off from Platform or Runtime owners and update examples across languages. Use canary deploy to 10% of traffic (docs feature flags) before full rollout.

Monitoring and Alerts

- Alerts to #devex-docs when quickstart CI fails >3 times in 24 hours.
- Docs site latency >500ms for health check -> P2 alert.
- Missing canonical fix for top-5 issue after 24 hours -> escalation to DevEx lead and customer-success.

Appendix: Templates and Examples

1) Quickstart README template (text form)
- TL;DR (1 line)
- Prereqs (SDK version, env vars)
- Steps (clone, install, set key, run)
- Expected output (copy/paste)
- Troubleshooting (links to canonical fixes)

2) Quick reference table (to be rendered in docs site)
- Columns: Template, Language, CI smoke, Owner
- Example row: Minimal API quickstart, Python, passes, devex-team@redwood.com

3) Example GitHub Actions snippet for validating quickstarts:
```yaml
name: Quickstart smoke
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - name: Install deps
        run: pip install -r quickstart/requirements.txt
      - name: Run smoke test
        run: python quickstart/run_smoke.py
```
